# Per-second enhanced_speed for the WORK LAPS of the two recordings #149 was
# argued from -- the SAME laps, in the same order, second for second, as
# scripts/fixtures/cue_work_laps.txt carries row_stroke_rate for. Read by
# scripts/speed_witness.py, which requires that alignment and refuses to publish
# a figure if the two files have drifted apart.
#
# WHY A SECOND FIXTURE RATHER THAN A COLUMN IN THE FIRST. cue_work_laps.txt is
# the display cue's input and its header promises "NOTHING BUT STROKE RATE IS
# HERE"; scripts/cue_replay.py consumes it positionally. Widening it would make
# every cue figure depend on a series the cue never sees.
#
# FORMAT
#   ROW <key> <label>               starts a row
#   LAP <v> <v> <v> ...             one work lap, one value per recorded second
#   Lines beginning with # and blank lines are ignored.
#
# 0 IS A REAL READING HERE, and that is the one way this file differs from its
# companion. In cue_work_laps.txt a 0 is the app's NO-DATA SENTINEL, because
# outputRate() returns 0.0 when nothing has been measured. enhanced_speed has no
# such convention: 0.000 m/s is a legal speed, and 34 calm / 30 choppy work-lap
# seconds carry exactly that. No second of either row is MISSING enhanced_speed,
# so this file needs no absence encoding at all -- which is stated rather than
# left to be noticed, because inventing one later would silently redefine the
# 0s already written here (#86 / #107).
#
# PROVENANCE, so this is reproducible from the originals with any FIT decoder:
#   source files   i171679853.fit (calm), i172336333.fit (choppy)
#   values         the 'enhanced_speed' field of record messages (FIT global
#                  message 20, field 73), in timestamp order, in m/s
#   lap boundaries lap messages (FIT global 19), start_time (field 2) inclusive
#                  to timestamp (field 253) exclusive
#   work laps      calm  -- total_elapsed_time (field 7) >= 600 s
#                          -> 4 laps, 3522 seconds
#                  choppy -- total_elapsed_time within 5 s of 180 s
#                          -> 8 laps, 1442 seconds
#                  (identical to cue_work_laps.txt's rule, which is what makes
#                  the two files align)
#   precision      enhanced_speed is a uint32 scaled by 1000, i.e. the file
#                  carries whole mm/s. Written here to 3 decimal places with
#                  trailing zeros stripped, so every value is EXACT -- no
#                  rounding was applied and none can move a figure.
#
# CROSS-CHECKS a reader can run against the originals in two minutes, all pinned
# by scripts/test_speed_witness.py:
#   calm   lap median speeds  2.387, 2.167, 1.951, 1.769 m/s   (over every
#   choppy lap median speeds  2.361, 2.439, 2.425, 2.590,       second of the
#                             2.466, 2.502, 2.325, 2.402 m/s    lap)
#   calm   min 0.000  max 2.806 m/s
#   choppy min 0.000  max 3.111 m/s
#
# THE CHOPPY ROW IS THE FASTER ONE, which looks wrong beside its lower stroke
# rates and is recorded here so nobody "corrects" it: the two rows are different
# days on different water, not a controlled pair. Nothing this fixture is used
# for compares the two rows' speeds to each other -- every figure
# speed_witness.py prints is a ratio WITHIN one row, against that row's own laps.
ROW calm 4x15' durability, calm water
